Article Title: Apple CEO John Ternus on how Steve Jobs’ ‘furniture story’ inspires product design at the company
Article Text:
The ‘carpenter's lesson’

Apple CEO John Ternus, who recently stepped into the top leadership position after guiding the company’s hardware engineering teams across multiple device generations, has shared how an iconic Steve Jobs philosophy continues to dictate Apple ’s design standards – even on its most budget-friendly devices. Speaking soon after the launch of the MacBook Neo earlier this year, Ternus revisited one of his favourite stories about the late Apple co-founder, illustrating how attention to unseen details remains the foundation of the company’s product line.Ternus recounted a quiet moment involving Jobs moving a bedroom dresser away from the wall.“Steve was moving a piece of furniture, a chest of drawers, and pulled it away from the wall and looked at the back and was just reflecting on the carpenter who had made it beautiful. It finished the back as beautifully as the rest of it, even though nobody was going to see it right and I think about that all the time because I think that perfectly exemplifies what we do here,” he said.The mindset of treating internal components and unseen surfaces with the same engineering precision as the exterior casing has been a foundational rule of Apple hardware since the earliest Macintosh models. Ternus connected that design ethos directly to the MacBook Neo, pointing out that cost-effective pricing does not mean cutting corners on aesthetic or structural integrity.“We've been talking about the MacBook Neo. Here is our most affordable Mac we've ever made, and it's absolutely beautiful. And if you open it up and look inside, it's just as beautiful,” Tetanus said.“And that's true about all products – an iPhone Pro Max or a MacBook Pro or an iPad Pro, but it's also true on a MacBook Neo,” he added, suggesting that Apple applies the exact same standards to its entry-level hardware.For Ternus, continuing to obsess over hidden details provides a clear roadmap for where the company is headed under his tenure.“That's what we do, and so, it's just been really good just to think about that and reflect on that because that is probably the best kind of clue as to where we're going in the future. We're going to keep pushing in that same way,” Ternus said.
Article Summary: Apple CEO John Ternus has shared how an iconic Steve Jobs philosophy continues to dictate Apple’s design standards. He recounted a quiet moment involving Jobs moving a bedroom dresser away from the wall. The mindset of treating internal components and unseen surfaces with the same engineering precision as the exterior casing has been a foundational rule of Apple hardware.

Article Title: India’s First Agentic AI Campus Takes Shape at KLH Hyderabad
Article Text: KLH Hyderabad today inaugurated its Agentic AI Campus initiative and signed an MoU with HCL Group AI Labs, unveiling a roadmap that places AI-powered learning and student innovation at the centre of its academic vision. The collaboration aims to equip students across disciplines to understand, build and apply intelligent technologies through practical projects, faculty mentorship and industry engagement. Mr. Deepak Sarvanan, National Head, HCL Group AI Labs, formally inaugurated the initiative at a press meet in KLH Bachupally campus in Hyderabad.Dr. L. Koteswara Rao, Principal, KLH Bachupally, represented KLH at the MoU exchange, alongside Dr. A. Srinath, Dean – Skill Development, in the presence of other senior officials, deans, faculty and staff.The initiative aims to make AI an integral part of the student experience. From exploring concepts in the classroom to developing applications, students will be encouraged to use AI to investigate problems, test ideas and create solutions relevant to industry and society.Er. Koneru Lakshman Havish, Vice President, KL Deemed to be University said, “We want students to develop the confidence and skills to shape how AI is used in their chosen fields.Our collaboration with HCL Group AI Labs will help connect classroom learning with hands-on projects and industry expertise, giving students opportunities to build intelligent solutions for real-world needs. As we develop our Agentic AI Campus, our focus is on preparing young people to innovate responsibly and contribute meaningfully to an evolving workplace. ”Agentic AI brings a new dimension to this approach. These systems can plan and carry out a series of tasks towards a defined goal, with appropriate human oversight. Understanding how such systems work will help students explore applications that extend from analysing information to coordinating workflows and supporting decisions.The proposed roadmap envisages project-based learning in areas such as business automation, data-driven services and discipline-specific AI applications. Students will be encouraged to design and test solutions, evaluating their accuracy, reliability and practical value.Faculty readiness will be a key part of the campus’s development. The collaboration envisages supporting educators in integrating AI into teaching, assignments and mentorship, helping students connect technical understanding with critical thinking and independent judgement.Responsible AI use will remain central to the learning approach, with attention to data privacy, bias, reliability and human accountability. Students will be encouraged to question outputs, verify information and understand the limitations of the systems they develop and use.Through its collaboration with HCL Group AI Labs, KLH Hyderabad aims to strengthen the connection between academic learning and the evolving workplace across its Bachupally and Aziznagar campuses, preparing students to develop AI solutions and apply them thoughtfully to real-world challenges.
Article Summary: KLH Hyderabad has signed an MoU with HCL Group AI Labs. The initiative aims to make AI an integral part of the student experience. Students will be encouraged to use AI to investigate problems, test ideas and create solutions relevant to industry and society.

Article Title: OpenAI to watermark ChatGPT and Codex text in Europe, here's what it means for users
Article Text:
What is changing

How the watermark works

Limits of detection

What it means for users

Who gets the detector

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI has announced that it will add invisible watermarks to text generated by ChatGPT and Codex for users in the European Union, as the company moves to comply with new requirements under the EU AI Act. The company also said that the rollout will being over the coming weeks and will apply to eligible ChatGPT and Codex text outputs across all plans in the EU. The move is designed to make AI-generated text identifiable in a machine-readable way while promoting greater transparency around AI-created content.OpenAI said that over the coming weeks it will add the watermark to eligible text output from ChatGPT and Codex. The change covers all plans in the EU and nowhere else. The company said it is not making text watermarking a global default at launch and described the regional approach as a way to learn from real-world use and feedback.The company is also making watermarking available to developers. Starting immediately, API customers worldwide can opt in to watermarked text for select models. It stays off by default in the API. OpenAI said it is working with cloud partners to offer watermarking for its models through their services in the coming weeks.OpenAI's technology, called textGrain, adds a statistical signal to the model's word choices. Readers cannot see it. A detector looks for that pattern to judge whether a passage carries an OpenAI watermark. OpenAI has published a technical report on the method and said it plans to release the technology as open source.The company said textGrain matched or beat the other approaches it tested, including SynthID for text. It added that strong results under ideal conditions do not guarantee reliable detection in everyday use.OpenAI's own evaluations show where the technology struggles:* Length matters. At a 1% false positive rate, the detector found watermarks in about 80% of 200-token passages and about 95% of 400-token passages in content such as psychology. Detection was substantially lower for content such as mathematics, where there is less flexibility in word choice.* Editing weakens the signal. In tests on 400-token passages, swapping 10% of words for synonyms cut detection from about 92% to 66%. Swapping 25% cut it to 17%.What a watermark does and does not showOpenAI listed several things a detection result cannot tell anyone:* It does not measure how much a human contributed to the text.* It does not establish who owns the text or who is responsible for it.* It does not identify the user. It does not link the text to a person, account, prompt or conversation.* It does not verify whether the text is accurate.* The absence of a watermark does not prove a human wrote the text. Short, edited or translated text may evade detection. Text may also come from an unsupported model, predate watermarking or come from another company's tools.For people using ChatGPT or Codex in the EU, the visible experience should not change, since the marker cannot be seen. OpenAI said it found no meaningful quality difference in tests of its latest frontier model, Astra, with and without watermarking. On eight benchmarks, the scores were close, with the watermarked version slightly ahead on some and slightly behind on others.Users should understand that a watermark is not a verdict on authorship. Because it can be weakened by editing and does not identify users, it is not a reliable way to prove who wrote a passage. That matters for anyone who might otherwise treat a detection result as proof, such as teachers, employers and publishers.OpenAI said the detector does not reveal users' prompts or conversations.OpenAI is not releasing the text detector to the public. Researchers and expert organizations can apply for access, which will be granted case by case under the EU's Code of Practice on AI-generated content. The company said the risk of missed watermarks and false positives is the reason it is holding back a public release.Its tools for images and audio remain publicly available. These include a web verification tool at openai.com/verify and a Content Provenance API.
Article Summary: ChatGPT-maker OpenAI will add invisible watermarks to text generated by ChatGPT and Codex for users in the European Union. The move is designed to make AI- generated text identifiable in a machine-readable way while promoting greater transparency around AI-created content.

Article Title: An American citizen was arrested at airport by Border security for wiping his phone with PIN; Federal judge approves search without warrant; here's what new ruling says on phone and laptop searches
Article Text:
Federal judge approves search without warrant; here's what new ruling says on phone and laptop searches

What the court said

What was the Atlanta case where man wiped his phone with PIN

Here’s what U.S. Customs and Border Protection said about border search of electronic devices at ports of entry

U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is responsible for protecting our nation’s borders and enforcing numerous laws at U.S.

ports of entry. CBP’s ability to lawfully inspect electronic devices crossing the border is integral to keeping America safe in an increasingly digital world.

All travelers crossing the United States border are subject to CBP inspection. On rare occasions, CBP officers may search a traveler’s mobile phone, computer, camera, or other electronic devices during the inspection process. These searches have been used to identify and combat terrorist activity, drug smuggling, human smuggling, bulk cash smuggling, human trafficking, intellectual property rights violations and visa fraud, among other violations.

They enable the discovery of digital contraband, such as child pornography, illicit transfer of restricted or classified information, or other export-controlled information. Furthermore, border searches of electronic devices are often integral to determining an individual’s intentions upon entry to the United States and thus provide additional information relevant to admissibility of foreign nationals under U.S.

immigration laws.

CBP has established strict guidelines, above and beyond prevailing legal requirements, to ensure that these searches are exercised judiciously and responsibly and are consistent with the public trust.

The number of travelers crossing the border that experience a border search of their electronic devices is small. In Fiscal Year (FY) 2025, less than 0.01 percent of arriving international travelers encountered by CBP at a port of entry had their electronic devices searched. Additional statistics are available in the Frequently Asked Questions below and Relevant Policies and Documents box to the right of this page.

US border agents can search people’s phones and other electronic devices without a warrant or any suspicion, a federal judge has ruled. In a ruling last month, the US Court of Appeals for the 2nd Circuit said that border agents do not need reasonable suspicion before manually searching a traveller's cellphone at the border. The ruling comes months after an Atlanta resident, Samuel Tunick was arrested on charges of destruction of property for wiping his phone with PIN during airport search. Prosecutors then accused Tunick of destroying potential evidence. The latest ruling stemmed from a bank fraud and money laundering case against a man in New York City in 2024.Writing in the 2nd Circuit’s majority opinion, Judge Steven J. Menashi said that border agents in the case stated above and others can “manually” look through someone’s phone or other device without needing to give a reason. In the ruling, Menashi said that there should be no distinction between a phone and other types of property, equating it to luggage or a notebook.“Because a cellphone is property, our precedents establish that the government does not need to have reasonable suspicion before searching a traveler’s cellphone at the border,” he wrote.As reported by The Guardian, Samuel Lutnick’s case centred on GrapheneOS, a custom Android operating system that runs in place of the software on most modern Google Pixel devices.These include the ability to erase a device by entering a designated passcode. The incident occurred at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport on January 24, after Tunick returned from the Dominican Republic. Tunick’s attorneys confirmed GrapheneOS was running on his phone.Agents repeatedly asked Tunick to unlock his phone and warned that it would be seized if he refused. After he eventually provided a passcode, “the screen went blank, flashed several times, and the phone appeared to restart,” according to the defence motion. Data stored on the device was subsequently lost.Prosecutors then alleged that the wipe was a deliberate attempt to destroy potential evidence. Tunick’s lawyers maintain that the underlying search violated his constitutional rights. The GrapheneOS has a feature that allows the device owner to set a passcode that deliberately wipes the contents of that device if entered instead of the user’s unlock passcode.
Article Summary: US border agents can search people’s phones and other electronic devices without a warrant or any suspicion. In a ruling last month, the US Court of Appeals for the 2nd Circuit said that border agents do not need reasonable suspicion before manually searching a traveller's cellphone at the border. The ruling comes months after an Atlanta resident, Samuel Tunick was arrested on charges of destruction of property for wiping his phone with PIN during airport search.

Article Title: Cab driver allegedly snatches farmer’s phone, transfers Rs 90,000
Article Text: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar: A cab driver allegedly snatched a 66-year-old farmer’s mobile phone and used a digital payment platform to siphon off Rs 90,000 from his bank account in three transactions, police said.Jawahar Nagar police registered an FIR against cab driver Deepak Simon Shelke and Kunal Deepak Shelke following a complaint by Dwarkadas Harinarayan Baheti, a resident of Kasliwal Marble in the Beed Bypass area.According to the complaint, the incident occurred near the Devi temple in Vishnunagar between 3.38pm on Oct 1 and 10am on Oct 2. Baheti alleged that Deepak forcibly snatched his Samsung Galaxy A15 phone.The accused allegedly accessed PhonePe on the phone and transferred Rs 90,000 in three transactions to a bank account held in Kunal’s name.Baheti told police that he could not lodge the complaint immediately as his wife was unwell. He approached police after her condition improved.Jawahar Nagar police are investigating the alleged roles of both the cab driver and the recipient of the money. Sub-inspector Kamble is conducting the probe.
Article Summary: Jawahar Nagar police registered an FIR against cab driver Deepak Simon Shelke and Kunal Deepak Shelke following a complaint. Dwarkadas Harinarayan Baheti, a resident of Kasliwal Marble in the Beed Bypass area, alleged that Deepak forcibly snatched his Samsung Galaxy A15.

Article Title: Round the clock ration to be available in Nashik with new grain ATM
Article Text:
Grain ATM to be launched by supply department in Nashik

Nashik

:





For ration card holders, collecting the monthly quota of wheat and rice often means planning the day around a visit to the ration shop. They have to arrive when the shop is open, wait in a queue and hope the e-PoS machine works. There are also complaints of receiving less grain than their entitlement.That routine could soon change in Nashik. In a first-of-its-kind initiative in Maharashtra , an automatic grain dispensing machine is expected to start functioning at Nashik Road by mid-Oct. Think of it as an ATM for foodgrain. Authenticate yourself, place your bag and collect your quota.More importantly, beneficiaries can do it at a time that suits them. The machine will operate 24x7, freeing families from ration shop timings and long waits. It is also expected to cut human intervention in weighing and dispensing grain, addressing complaints of short-weighing.The food and civil supplies department is setting up the facility on a pilot basis at the old govt foodgrain warehouse at Nashik Road. Nagpur is also among the state’s pioneer centres selected for the experiment.“The initiative aims to address recurring operational issues faced by beneficiaries under the PDS, including frequent technical glitches in e-PoS machines, erratic shop hours, long waiting times and complaints regarding short-weighing,” officiating district supply officer Ramesh Gaikwad said.The machine can store 100 quintals of grain, with 50 quintals each of wheat and rice.For beneficiaries, the process is designed to be simple.They will enter their Aadhaar or ration card number and authenticate their identity through a fingerprint scan. Their entitlement will appear on the screen. Once verified, the machine will automatically measure and release the grain into their bag.It can dispense up to 50kg within five minutes, officials said.The facility will cater to beneficiaries under the Antyodaya Anna Yojana and Priority Household schemes. Migrant workers covered by the One Nation One Ration Card system can also use it, removing geographical restrictions on where they collect their grain.That could make the system particularly useful for workers whose schedules often clash with ration shop hours.Solar power backup is another feature intended to keep the machine running during electricity outages. Local ration dealers will oversee the facility and refill wheat and rice when stocks run low.The experiment does not, however, eliminate ration shops altogether. The automated unit is meant specifically for free grain and does not have a payment facility. If govt announces items that have to be purchased, including supplies distributed under special schemes, those will continue to require a fair price shop dealer to collect payment and hand over the goods.
Article Summary: Machine will operate 24x7, freeing families from ration shop timings and long waits. It is also expected to cut human intervention in weighing and dispensing grain, addressing complaints of short-weighing. Facility will cater to beneficiaries under Antyodaya Anna Yojana and Priority Household schemes.

Article Title: Spain turned a traffic roundabout into a public bath; the 6-day experiment was later named a climate refuge
Article Text:
Representative Image of a vibrant public bath in a traffic roundabout, complete with steam rooms and cold-water basins (AI Generated Image)

Round About Baths turned a traffic island into a temporary public bath

The climate reason behind a bath in a traffic roundabout

A temporary experiment in changing how cities use space

In Logroño, Spain, a traffic roundabout was temporarily transformed into a public bath, turning a space normally dominated by passing cars into a place for bathing and gathering. Called Round About Baths, the installation was designed by Leopold Banchini Architects for the 2025 edition of the Concéntrico architecture and design festival. Built around an existing fountain at the roundabout at Plaza Salón, on Gran Vía, the project added changing rooms, a steam room and cold-water basins behind timber walls. The installation operated from June 19 to 24, 2025, before the temporary structure was removed. Its unusual setting was part of the point: the project challenged the conventional role of road infrastructure by temporarily turning a car-dominated space into a place for people. The project's official European Prize for Urban Public Space profile also describes it as a temporary climate refuge for cases of extreme heat.The project began with the roundabout itself. According to Concéntrico's project description, the fountain at the centre was visible but inaccessible to pedestrians because of the surrounding traffic.The architects temporarily surrounded it with the facilities required for a public bath, creating an enclosed space inside an otherwise inaccessible part of the city. Leopold Banchini Architects designed the installation using a timber structure clad with uncut wooden panels. The arrangement included changing rooms, a steam room and cold-water basins, creating a sequence that moved visitors from the heated interior space to the outdoor area where they could cool down.The project was not simply an installation to be viewed from outside. For the period in which it operated, it functioned as a public bathing facility. According to the official user guide, sessions lasted 45 minutes, capacity was limited, and visitors entered in timed slots. Participants were required to bring their own towel and wear a bathing suit. The experience began in the hot steam room before continuing outdoors, where visitors could rest and cool down in the cold-water basins. The installation also had rules intended to preserve privacy and make the unusual setting workable. Changing areas were positioned on either side of the entrance, while personal belongings were placed in individual bags and held by staff during each session. Children under five were not permitted to enter, and users were asked to maintain silence, respect and considerate behaviour.The project's climate dimension becomes clearer in its later recognition by the European Prize for Urban Public Space. The prize's official project description calls Round About Baths a temporary public bath and “climate refuge” for cases of extreme heat, saying that it challenges the meaning of road infrastructure by turning space intended for vehicles into a place where people can meet at a human scale. That framing does not mean the installation was presented as a permanent solution to extreme heat. It was an ephemeral architectural project that operated for only a few days. Instead, its climate function was tied to the way water and bathing could temporarily change how people experienced an urban space during periods of heat.The design also made use of an existing piece of infrastructure rather than requiring an entirely new site. The fountain, which had previously been visible but inaccessible, became part of a functioning public bath. High timber walls provided privacy from the surrounding traffic, while the steam room and cold-water basins created spaces for heating and cooling within the temporary structure. The festival's own description also emphasises the project's broader urban argument. It says the installation revealed the hidden potential of a car-dominated environment by temporarily repurposing street equipment and changing how people perceived a forgotten space.Round About Baths was designed to be reversible. The tall walls were made from a regular timber structure and uncut wooden panels that were intended to have a second life after the festival. Once the temporary installation was removed, the fountain could return to its previous state. That reversibility was important to the project's architectural approach. Instead of permanently rebuilding a traffic junction, the intervention temporarily tested a completely different use for it. A space normally experienced from inside a passing car became a destination where people could stop, change clothes, enter a steam room and cool themselves in water.The project was subsequently selected as one of the five finalists for the 2026 European Prize for Urban Public Space, which recognises projects that create, recover or transform public space in European cities. The official prize profile places Round About Baths among projects exploring how urban infrastructure can be reconsidered for human and environmental needs. For several days in June 2025, therefore, the centre of a Spanish traffic roundabout was no longer simply something drivers passed around. It became a functioning public bath and, in the framing of the European Prize for Urban Public Space, a temporary refuge from extreme heat. The experiment was short-lived, but its central question was broader: whether infrastructure built primarily for cars can also be adapted, even temporarily, to provide spaces for people, water, cooling and communal life.
Article Summary: The installation was designed by Leopold Banchini Architects for the 2025 edition of the Concéntrico architecture and design festival. Built around an existing fountain, the project added changing rooms, a steam room and cold-water basins behind timber walls. The installation operated from June 19 to 24, 2025, before the temporary structure was removed.

Article Title: Satellites map nearly 2,000 valleys and a buried mountain range beneath Greenland ice, revealing a vast subglacial network across the ice sheet
Article Text:
Image AI generated

Why does BedMachine Greenland have gaps in subglacial valley mapping

How did researchers map 1,943 subglacial valleys

What did researchers find beneath Greenland’s ice

How could 3,031 branching angles reveal Greenland’s past climate

Beneath the Greenland Ice Sheet lies a vast, island-wide network of valleys. The team applied Ice Flow Perturbation Analysis to surface elevation and velocity observations and manually mapped 1,943 subglacial valleys, 34% of which are not present in BedMachine Greenland. According to a paper published in Geophysical Research Letters titled ‘A Vast Valley Network Beneath the Greenland Ice Sheet ’, the network covers 74% of the ice sheet, compared with 39% in BedMachine. They also describe a subglacial mountain range south-east of the Northeast Greenland Ice Stream. In their view, the valleys' orientation and branching angles point to tectonic inheritance and a long-term groundwater influence.According to the study, mapping the bed along the margin of the Greenland Ice Sheet was transformed by reconciling measurements of ice thickness and surface velocity using the principle of mass conservation. The authors write that this method cannot be applied to the slower-flowing interior, where ice thickness observations are sparse. In the plain language summary, they say it leaves three-quarters of the ice sheet with poorly resolved bedrock topography. For the 150-metre-resolution BedMachine Greenland product, only 4.4% of ice-sheet grid cells include a radar observation.The interior and slower-flowing margins of that product are unrealistically smooth compared with the periphery, but pockmarked along survey lines by sparsely sampled valleys.The authors note that ice flow and subglacial water drainage tend to focus toward such valleys. Their alternative uses the fact that significant bumps and troughs in the bed can produce detectable variations on the surface. The method relies on bed-to-surface signal transfer theory and fine-resolution maps of surface elevation and velocity. It was developed by Ockenden and colleagues for Antarctica and is modified here for Greenland. According to the paper, the inputs are the GrIMP version 2 digital elevation model and the MEaSUREs Multi-year Greenland Ice Sheet Velocity Mosaic. Both are resampled onto the 150-metre BedMachine grid, and ice thickness comes from BedMachine Greenland version 6.The researchers traced valley centrelines by hand at a scale of 1:750,000. They focused on valleys at least 10 kilometres long and 1 kilometre wide, the same criteria used by MacGregor and colleagues in 2024. The paper reports 1,943 mapped subglacial valleys. Of these, 34% are identified by the new method and are not present in BedMachine. The authors add that 52% of the valleys visible in BedMachine are extended farther by the new method. They state that many valleys resolved by mass conservation along the periphery extend much farther inland, sometimes hundreds of kilometres more than in BedMachine.Subglacial valleys confine the flow of nearly all of Greenland's 239 largest outlet glaciers, those with termini at least 1.5 kilometres wide. Most of these, about 70%, are extended farther upstream in the blended topography. According to the authors, most that are not extended lie in the south-east drainage basin and are relatively small, with discharge below 1 gigatonne per year. Based on mapped valley presence in a 10-kilometre grid, the paper reports that the areal extent of the valley network is nearly doubled in the blended topography, at 74% of the ice sheet, compared with 39% in BedMachine. The authors say this extent is limited mainly by where the blended map does not use the new method, mostly because of disrupted basal units in the northern ice sheet.The authors write that their analyses are consistent with the hypothesis that alpine-style subglacial geomorphology dominates the region south-east of the Northeast Greenland Ice Stream and next to the eastern highlands. BedMachine only hints at substantial relief there. The new method reveals a subglacial mountain range with an interconnected valley network, with increasingly greater relief to the east. The authors state that this network spans the transition from a likely frozen bed to the south to a likely thawed bed to the north, closer to the ice stream. They add that several deeply incised valleys slope approximately radially inland from this region. They describe these as preferential pathways for past subglacial or glaciofluvial erosion beneath what is now slow-moving and likely cold-based ice.In far southern Greenland, the paper says the new method also generates rough subglacial topography. There the ice is presumed to be warmer, and firn aquifers are more common, which limits the success of radar sounding and leaves BedMachine unnaturally smooth. The study reports that the subglacial southern highlands have similar relief to the coastal regions, and that this relief extends north into a valley network less clearly visible in either the surface or BedMachine. Automated mapping outlined 22 larger dendritic basins, each over 10,000 square kilometres. In southern Greenland, below 68°N, these basins coalesce around the southern highlands. Most basins farther north coalesce toward the eastern highlands. One of the two largest basins terminates at Sermeq Kujalleq (Jakobshavn Isbræ). The authors say their network differs from that of Cooper and colleagues in 2016, since the southern highlands feed Akuliarutsip Sermia, about 100 kilometres to its south-west, rather than Sermeq Kujalleq.The authors analysed valley orientation using Hough transforms across 75-kilometre squares. They report a typically bimodal distribution of azimuths by drainage basin. South-west to north-east is most common in the CW, NW, NE and CE basins. South-east to north-west is next most common, in the SW, NW and SE basins. These orientations bear no clear relation to modern ice-flow directions. The study links the dominant south-west to north-east azimuth to a left-lateral shear pattern proposed by Beh in 1975. That proposal came with a "Wegener Fault" in Nares Strait, which the paper says was discarded once geological and structural observations precluded the fault. The authors state that parts of Greenland's plate may still have experienced shear after the Late Cretaceous, and that valleys may later have exploited this tectonic inheritance. They add that GNSS stations record differences in horizontal plate motion directions that are presently unresolved. 3,031 branching angles in the valley network, with a distribution peaking between about 50 and 65 degrees. This range is diagnostic of climates where groundwater flow or soil erosion are non-negligible but smaller contributors to channel incision than precipitation or surface runoff. They write that it implies an aridity index of about 0.1 to 1 during valley incision. Slipperiness is set to a uniform value over most of the ice sheet, which the authors say is unlikely to be accurate. However, varying it only changes the amplitude of the perturbations, so they are confident in the locations of the valleys if not their absolute relief. Disrupted basal units in the north prevented use of the method in places, and the authors highlight these regions as possible targets for future airborne radar surveys.
Article Summary: Researchers used AI to map 1,943 subglacial valleys, 34% of which are not present in BedMachine Greenland. The network covers 74% of the ice sheet, compared with 39% in Bed machine. The researchers traced valley centrelines by hand at a scale of 1:750,000 and focused on valleys at least 10 kilometres long and 1km wide.

Article Title: In 1916, the US began releasing Asian lady beetles to control aphids and scale insects; decades later Harmonia axyridis became invasive and was linked to declines of native ladybirds
Article Text:
lady beetle

An import meant to help farmers

The first wild populations

Asian lady beetles

A familiar beetle with many faces

When helpful became harmful

A difficult species to control

A nuisance in homes too

Lessons from a century-old decision

The multicoloured Asian lady beetle was introduced to the United States with a clear purpose. Starting as early as 1916, agricultural officials released the insect, scientifically known as Harmonia axyridis, in an effort to control aphids, scale insects and other crop pests without relying as heavily on chemical insecticides. It was an appealing form of biological control, but the story took an unexpected turn. After the species established wild populations in the late 1980s, it spread rapidly across the country and beyond, becoming one of the world’s most successful invasive insects. According to reports by the USDA Agricultural Research Service, it can outcompete native ladybirds and is now regarded as an invasive species in many regions.The multicoloured Asian lady beetle is native to Asia, where it feeds on aphids and other soft-bodied arthropods. Those feeding habits made it attractive to US agricultural researchers looking for natural ways to control pests in orchards, forests, gardens and field crops. Aphids can damage plants by extracting sap, while scale insects can weaken trees and shrubs, so a predator that consumed large numbers of these pests appeared to be a useful ally.Federal, state and private entomologists released Harmonia axyridis at several locations over the years. The beetles were meant to reduce pest populations and, in turn, lower the need for insecticides. In some settings, that promise was fulfilled, especially in pecan orchards and on ornamental plants, where the beetles helped control aphids.At the time, biological control was widely viewed as a practical alternative to chemical pest management. Introducing predators can offer benefits when the predator remains focused on its target prey and fits into the new ecosystem without causing disruption. The challenge is that ecosystems are complex, and an insect that is helpful in one place can behave very differently after crossing continents.Although releases began as early as 1916, the first established US populations of multicoloured Asian lady beetles were not documented until 1988. They were found in Louisiana near the busy port of New Orleans, far from many of the locations where planned releases had occurred. That gap raised a key question: did the species establish because of intentional releases, accidental introductions through trade, or both?USDA researchers note that accidental entries likely occurred through imported nursery stock at ports in Delaware and South Carolina. This makes it difficult to trace the exact origin of the invasion. What is clear is that once Harmonia axyridis gained a foothold, it spread rapidly through North America and later across other continents.The beetle’s success was helped by its adaptability. It can survive in orchards, forests, row crops, gardens and urban areas, feeding on a broad range of prey. It also reproduces quickly, with development from egg to adult taking roughly 15 to 25 days depending on temperature and food availability. These traits gave it a major advantage in new habitats, as per the reports.The Asian lady beetle can be difficult to identify because its appearance varies greatly. Its wing covers may range from black to mustard yellow or red, and the number of spots can vary from none to many. In the United States, a common form is mustard to red with 16 or more black spots, but the diversity in colour and markings means it is not always easy to distinguish from native species at a glance.Like other ladybirds, it goes through four distinct life stages: egg, larva, pupa and adult. Females begin laying eggs on host plants in early spring, and the larvae immediately begin hunting aphids and other soft-bodied prey after hatching. Both adults and larvae are active predators, meaning the species can have a strong effect on insect populations wherever it becomes abundant.That feeding efficiency is exactly what made the beetle valuable to agriculture. However, a voracious appetite is not limited to crop pests. It can also put pressure on native ladybirds that depend on the same food sources, turning an agricultural helper into a conservation concern.The USDA describes the Asian lady beetle as a mixed blessing. It remains an effective predator of aphids and other pests, but has also become a nuisance in homes and a threat to biodiversity. In invaded countries Harmonia axyridis is considered invasive as it can outcompete other ladybug species for food and habitat.Native ladybugs might be unable to compete with a highly adaptable newcomer moving into the same ecological niche. Harmonia axyridis is larger than many native species, highly mobile and able to use a wide range of habitats. Its ability to find food across different crops and landscapes can give it an advantage when prey is scarce.The beetle also has strong defences. USDA research notes that it possesses chemical, mechanical and microbiological anti-predator traits that cause many predators to avoid it. These defences reduce the natural pressure that might otherwise limit its numbers, allowing populations to increase and spread.Scientists have studied whether predators and parasitoids could naturally slow the Asian lady beetle’s expansion. The evidence suggests that many vertebrate and invertebrate predators in invaded regions are relatively ineffective at limiting the beetle. Some birds and insects can consume it, but its defensive adaptations often make it an unappealing or difficult target.Parasitoids, organisms that develop on or inside a host and ultimately kill it, may offer some potential. USDA researchers identified certain true flies in the genus Phalacrotophora as possible natural enemies capable of overcoming some of the beetle’s defences. However, researchers stress that more work is needed to understand whether these relationships can meaningfully reduce populations at a larger scale.The case of Harmonia axyridis illustrates a common pattern in biological invasions. A species introduced without its full set of predators, parasites and ecological constraints may initially flourish. Over time, native species may adapt and new relationships may form, but that process can take years or decades and may not undo the harm already caused.For homeowners, the most visible problem often arrives in autumn. As temperatures drop, adult Asian lady beetles seek sheltered places to overwinter, including homes, sheds and other buildings. They are particularly drawn to light-coloured structures, such as white, grey and yellow houses, which can act as visual cues for the insects.The beetles do not damage structures in the way termites or carpenter ants do. They do not chew wood, bore through walls, feed on carpets, or lay eggs indoors. However, they can gather in large numbers in wall spaces and then enter living areas on warm winter or early spring days while searching for an exit.When disturbed or crushed, the insects can release a yellow, unpleasant-smelling fluid from their leg joints as a defence called reflex bleeding. The fluid can stain walls and fabrics, making the beetles unwelcome indoors despite being pest predators. USDA guidance recommends sealing cracks and crevices outside homes before autumn and using a vacuum or broom to remove beetles that get inside.The Asian lady beetle’s journey from a planned pest-control import to a widespread invasive species offers an important lesson about ecological caution. Biocontrol reduces pesticide use and protects crops, but all nonnative species come with risks that aren’t always immediately apparent. A predator may control one pest while competing with native species or creating new problems elsewhere.More than a century after the first US releases, Harmonia axyridis remains both useful and disruptive. It still has some use controlling aphids in certain agricultural settings, but the unintended consequences of its spread have come at a cost to native ladybugs and home comfort. Its history is a warning that even well-meaning attempts to help the environment have to be assessed not just on the benefits they bring in the short term, but on what they might lead to in the longer term. The experience also shows how difficult it can be to reverse the effects of an introduced species once it becomes firmly established in a new environment.
Article Summary: The multicoloured Asian lady beetle is native to Asia, where it feeds on aphids and other soft-bodied arthropods. In the late 1980s, the species established wild populations in the US. It spread rapidly across the country and beyond, becoming one of the world’s most successful invasive insects. According to reports by the USDA Agricultural Research Service, it can outcompete native ladybirds.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.
Article Summary: Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.

Article Title: Second Vande Bharat sleeper set to launch this month between Bengaluru and Mumbai; cutting travel time from 24 hours to under 16 hours, 30 year wait for faster connectivity between two cities to end
Article Text:
For more than 30 years, passengers have been seeking faster rail connectivity between Bengaluru and Mumbai.

Mumbai-Bengaluru Vande Bharat Sleeper: Expected Travel Time

What makes Vande Bharat sleeper special?

Vande Bharat sleeper: Indian Railways is all set to roll out the second Vande Bharat sleeper train after launching the first pair between Guwahati and Howrah earlier this year.After prolonged delays, the Railway Board is expected to issue the notification for the KSR Bengaluru-Mumbai CSMT Vande Bharat Sleeper shortly. According to sources, the train is likely to be flagged off later this month.The country's second Vande Bharat sleeper service is expected to substantially reduce the time taken to travel by rail between Bengaluru, India's technology hub, and Mumbai, its financial capital.Also Read | With better than Rajdhani experience & 160 kmph speed, can Vande Bharat sleeper trains be a game-changer for Indian Railways? Under the proposed schedule, the premium train will run six days a week in each direction, covering the distance in under 16 hours. At present, the Udyan Express, the only direct daily train connecting the two cities, takes an average of 24 hours to complete the journey.As per the tentative timings, the service may leave KSR Bengaluru at 10 PM and arrive at Mumbai CSMT at 1:50 PM the next day. On the return journey, it could start from Mumbai at 10:30 PM, reaching Bengaluru at 1:50 PM the following day. These are tentative timings and are subject to change.Although the official launch date has not yet been declared, the railway zones have been asked to commence the service at the earliest convenient opportunity.Its scheduled halts will include Anantapur, Guntakal, Raichur, Kalaburagi, Solapur and Kalyan, according to this TOI report For more than 30 years, passengers have been seeking faster rail connectivity between Bengaluru and Mumbai. Despite repeated assurances, train journeys between the two cities continue to take considerable time.The proposed Vande Bharat Sleeper service is expected to address this long-standing demand and improve connectivity between the cities.The Vande Bharat sleeper train has 16 passenger coaches. The rake includes 11 AC 3-tier coaches, four AC 2-tier coaches and one AC First Class coach.The train has been designed to operate at speeds of up to 160 kmph, while its testing speed is 180 kmph, placing it in the semi-high-speed category. However, most sections of the Indian Railways network are not equipped to permit trains to operate at such high speeds.Drawing on design elements seen in European trains, the Vande Bharat sleeper coaches feature cushioned berths aimed at providing greater comfort. The design of the upper berths has also been modified to make climbing up easier for passengers.Passenger amenities include dedicated night lights, integrated public announcement systems accompanied by visual displays, CCTV cameras and modular pantry units.The sleeper train is also equipped with modern bio-vacuum toilets similar to those used in aircraft. A separate toilet designed for disabled passengers also has a baby care station. Passengers travelling in AC First Class additionally have access to shower facilities with hot water.For safety, the Vande Bharat sleeper train comes fitted with the indigenous KAVACH anti-collision system. Like the chair car versions of Vande Bharat, the sleeper variant will also use regenerative braking technology to improve energy efficiency.Automatic interconnecting doors have been provided between the coaches. The gangways are fully sealed, helping maintain clean air inside the train as well as effective temperature control.Passenger convenience features in every coach include individual reading lights, charging points and refreshment tables. The interiors use GFRP panels. The train doors are designed to open automatically at designated stations.The train also comes with a Centralised Coach Monitoring System. An emergency communication facility allows passengers to communicate directly with the driver when required.Meanwhile, ICF is also working on developing its own version of the Vande Bharat sleeper train.
Article Summary: The KSR Bengaluru-Mumbai CSMT Vande Bharat Sleeper is likely to be flagged off later this month. The premium train will run six days a week in each direction, covering the distance in under 16 hours. At present, the Udyan Express, the only direct daily train connecting the two cities, takes an average of 24 hours.

We grew up with “Intel Inside” stickers on our PCs, a branding that made an invisible component a household symbol of trust and raw performance. Yet recent years brought turbulence, with rivals like Qualcomm squeezing Intel’s core market. Today, under the leadership of Lip-Bu Tan, the turnaround seems real. Backed by Washington and crucial partnerships with titans like Nvidia, Intel is regaining its operational stride. The legacy chipmaker launched the Core Ultra Series 3 processors (codenamed Panther Lake) at this year’s CES as Intel's first mobile platform built on the advanced Intel 18A process node – its biggest process innovation – making a strong case for its Core Ultra Series 3 processors in the AI PC race.Given the data in the public domain, the company’s chips hold a clear advantage over its competitors like Qualcomm’s Snapdragon platform – which compete in the same domain – in three areas: software and enterprise compatibility, real-world workloads like gaming and technologies that only Intel offers. Here is what Intel offers.Intel Core Ultra Series 3 processors are built on the x86 architecture. This essentially means the full Windows and Chrome OS software ecosystem runs natively on them, with no emulation and no workarounds.For businesses, Intel says this brings native compatibility with decades-old business applications or software, established security agents and enterprise management tools. It also covers the range of peripheral devices that organisations already use.Intel vPro adds another layer on top. According to the company, it gives IT teams a hardware-based way to remotely manage, secure and support devices across large fleets. This includes out-of-band management that works independently of the operating system. Intel describes it as a capability built and tested over years of enterprise use, and one of its strongest selling points for corporate PC buyers.Intel also points to its AI PC platform, which it says supports more than 500 optimised AI models. The company says over 100 independent software vendors (ISVs) are engaged in optimising software for AI PCs.On the performance side, Intel says Core Ultra Series 3 delivers up to 180 TOPS of total AI compute. This comes from the CPU, GPU and NPU working together. The company explains that this mixed design sends each AI workload to the most efficient processing engine for the job, instead of depending on one type of processor. In practice, Intel says this keeps performance steady when several tasks run at once, such as content creation, AI inferencing, video calls and background processes.Gaming is another area Intel highlights. Its x86 architecture works with the full Windows gaming ecosystem. That includes anti-cheat software, older titles, specialised controllers and peripheral drivers. Intel says these are areas where mobile-first architectures still face compatibility gaps.Intel also has a few technologies that set its platform apart.Integration of these standards delivers up to 120 Gbps of bandwidth. It supports fast data transfer, daisy-chained displays and universal docking. Intel says this is supported natively across its platforms but is not available on mobile-first architectures.This enables hardware-accelerated video encoding and decoding directly on the processor. Intel says content creators working with high-resolution footage get faster export times, without the CPU load that software encoding demands.
Article Summary: Intel Core Ultra Series 3 processors are built on the x86 architecture. Article Title: Facebook tests Reels-style full-screen video as it prepares new apps for sellers and creators
Article Text:
Facebook tests Reels-style full-screen video as it prepares new apps for sellers and creators

Facebook tests a video-first experience

Facebook launches Seller app for frequent sellers

Meta-owned Facebook is testing a new full-screen video experience that could change what users see when they open the app. The company said it will begin testing the video-first experience later this year, putting some users directly into full-screen video instead of the usual Feed. The app brings several selling tools together in one place. These include:- AI-powered listing creation- A unified inbox- Inventory management- Performance insightsThe app will remain connected to Facebook, meaning sellers can continue reaching buyers and their communities through the same network. Facebook said the goal is to make selling easier for people who list large numbers of products.
Article Summary: Facebook tests Reels-style full-screen video as it prepares new apps for sellers and creators. The move comes as Facebook marks 10 years of Marketplace and launches new tools for sellers, including a separate app called Seller. The company's Classic Feed will remain available as a second tab.

Visit an Aadhaar Seva Kendra or Aadhaar Enrolment/Update Centre. the process requires an in-person visit; it is not currently available end-to-end online for most categories of name change.

Fill out the Aadhaar Enrolment/Update form, writing the name in block letters, free of titles, aliases, or unapproved abbreviations.

Submit the prescribed supporting documents based on the specific category the request falls under — ranging from a simple PoI for minor corrections to a mandatory Gazette Notification for a major name change.

Complete identity verification and biometric authentication at the centre as part of the same visit.

Pay the applicable demographic update fee, currently listed by UIDAI at ₹75 when a name update is processed as a standalone request.

Collect the acknowledgement receipt, which includes an Update Request Number (URN) that can be used to track the status of the request online afterward.

UIDAI (Unique Identification Authority of India) has issued a revised Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for updating names in Aadhaar. The authority has introduced separate rules and documents requirements depending on the type of name change being requested. The new SOP, which came into effect on September 18, 2026, replaces the earlier process introduced in 2021. The updated procedure categorises requests into multiple categories, including minor spelling corrections, data-entry errors, surname changes after marriage or divorce, regional-language corrections and major name changes. According to UIDAI, documents, affidavits and Gazette notifications submitted with requests will be subject to stricter verification to prevent misuse and identity-related fraud.Under the revised SOP, names recorded in Aadhaar must appear in block letters, with no titles, prefixes (such as Shri, Smt, Ms, Dr, or Prof), aliases, ranks, or special characters permitted. Updates are governed under Regulation 19 of the Aadhaar (Enrolment & Update) Regulations, 2016, and any name change must be backed by documents listed under Schedule II. A name will be updated exactly as it appears — in spelling, sequence, and abbreviation — in the document the applicant submits as proof.UIDAI treats several routine corrections as minor name changes, requiring only standard Proof of Identity (PoI), or Proof of Relationship (PoR) for children under 18:These are accepted as long as the new name matches a PoI or PoR document the applicant has already submitted to UIDAI in the past.A separate category covers cases where the English spelling of a name on Aadhaar is correct, but the regional-language version contains an error — for instance, निर्मला being incorrectly recorded as निर्मल. These cases also require a standard PoI document to correct.Special cases with dedicated requirementsThe SOP carves out specific documentation paths for several commonly occurring situations:The strictest category under the new SOP covers a complete change of name or identity — for example, Ram Gupta becoming Shyam Gupta, or a more substantial identity shift. For these cases, UIDAI will accept only a Gazette Notification as proof, alongside standard identity documents; no other form of documentation is considered sufficient. The authority will also cross-check the proposed new name against every name previously recorded for that Aadhaar holder, and verify the authenticity of the Gazette Notification and any affidavits submitted.Under UIDAI's existing framework, a person can generally update their Aadhaar name twice in total. Once that limit is exhausted, any further name change requests must go through a separate exception-handling process. For context, gender on Aadhaar can typically be changed only once, and date of birth only once as well, under separate SOPs UIDAI maintains for those fields.To apply for a name correction or change under the new SOP, applicants need to follow a set sequence of steps:

The new SOP, which came into effect on September 18, 2026, replaces the earlier process introduced in 2021. The updated procedure categorises requests into multiple categories, including minor spelling corrections, data- entry errors and surname changes after marriage or divorce.

Article Title: As Google and SpaceX plan to solve the 'data centers problem' by taking them to the Sun; some researchers in Japan and Germany want to fix it right on Earth, and their solution is ...
Article Text:
AI-generated image for representation

How elastocaloric cooling works

How elastocaloric cooling can help data centers

Technology is still at the proof-of-concept stage

Data centers are putting increasing pressure on power grids as demand for computing continues to grow. Some companies are exploring alternatives such as solar-powered facilities while tech giants like Google and SpaceX are even planning to move data centers away from Earth. Recently, Google launched its homegrown AI chips into orbit aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket as part of Project Suncatcher, its effort to develop solar-powered AI computing infrastructure in space. The launch marked the project's first in-orbit test, which aims to use continuously available solar power and the “infinite real estate” of orbit for AI computing.As this approach explores moving computing infrastructure off-planet, researchers in Japan and Germany are working on a way to tackle the data center cooling problem without leaving Earth. Their solution uses shape memory alloy films in a system called “elastocaloric cooling.” The technology, known as “elastocaloric cooling,” uses a titanium-nickel alloy film that changes shape in response to heat and drives a refrigeration cycle. The study, published in Nature Energy, presents a prototype that could eventually find applications in data centers and other computing devices, although the current system remains at the proof-of-concept stage.The prototype consists of a thermal actuator and a cooling unit. Its thermal actuator uses a shape memory alloy film made from titanium-nickel. When the film reaches a sufficiently high temperature, it stretches and generates force that elongates a separate refrigerant film.The refrigerant film eventually contacts a heat sink, which removes heat from the film. As the actuator and refrigerant films cool, they return to their original shapes. The refrigerant film then contacts the heat source and absorbs heat, restarting the cycle.According to the researchers, the cooling process takes place through four steps involving the heating, deformation, cooling and recovery of the films. The system is designed to repeat the process continuously without requiring a conventional motor to drive the cooling operation.The research paper does not specifically propose the technology for data center cooling. However, the approach could potentially address one of the challenges associated with large computing facilities: the energy and water required to keep hardware within operating temperatures.Data centers use substantial amounts of electricity, while conventional cooling systems can add to their energy requirements. Some cooling systems also use water. A cooling technology based on shape memory alloy films could potentially reduce the need for some conventional cooling infrastructure if it can be scaled.The same principle could also have applications beyond large data centers, including personal computers and other electronic devices.The prototype currently has significant limitations. The researchers reported that the films generated only **2.09 milliwatts of cooling power**. The system was also limited by relatively slow actuation and the size of its heat exchanger.These limitations mean the technology is not yet ready to replace the cooling systems used in large computing facilities. Scaling cooling output while improving the system's speed and efficiency would be necessary before practical applications become possible.Still, the research demonstrates that elastocaloric cooling can work using shape-changing films rather than conventional motor-driven refrigeration. If researchers can overcome the current limitations, the approach could eventually offer another way to manage heat in computing hardware, including the increasingly power-hungry systems used in AI data centers.
Article Summary: Researchers in Japan and Germany are working on a way to tackle the data center cooling problem without leaving Earth. Their solution uses shape memory alloy films in a system called “elastocaloric cooling.” The technology, known as ‘elast vocaloric cooling,’ uses a titanium-nickel alloy film that changes shape in response to heat. The study presents a prototype that could eventually find applications in data centers.

Article Title: Elon Musk confirms talks with TSMC for Terafab chipmaking collaboration, says just discussions, but …
Article Text:
How the deal may work

Looming questions over Intel’s role

Elon Musk has confirmed that his companies are in active discussions with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) regarding a potential partnership for his Terafab semiconductor manufacturing. The confirmation comes as a report claimed that the talks explore establishing a dedicated chip manufacturing plant focused entirely on supplying Musk’s companies, including Tesla, SpaceX and artificial intelligence (AI) startup xAI.Musk acknowledged the engagement in a brief post on X (formerly Twitter), however, he downplayed anything concrete at the moment.“Just discussions, but something may come of it,” Musk wrote.He also replied, “True”, to a post which claimed that:“Anything TSMC contributes to Terafab would basically be supplemental. Terafab itself is going to be absurdly massive. The goal is 1 TW of compute production every year.....around 50× the current global output of AI compute. This isn’t just another fab. It’s being built for a scale the semiconductor industry simply does not operate at any known scale today.”Citing Tim Culpan’s Culpium newsletter which first claimed the potential collaboration, Tom’s Hardware reported that there may be two prospective operating models for the Terafab facility.Under the first plan, TSMC would directly own and run the fab. SpaceX or Terafab would contribute capital investments, sign binding minimum chip purchase agreements, or combine both commitments.Under the second plan, SpaceX may be granted majority control of the joint entity. TSMC would supply smaller capital injections while licensing proprietary process technologies and offering hands-on operational leadership.Background insights highlighted by Culpium suggest that persistent industry rumours regarding TSMC eyeing a chip fabrication complex in Texas may be closely linked to supporting the Terafab project.The emergence of TSMC may introduce major uncertainty around Intel's existing ties to Terafab. Currently, Intel is slated to deliver its 1.4-nanometer-class Intel 14A process node to manufacture semiconductors for SpaceX, Tesla and xAI under the Terafab banner. According to Tom’s Hardware, if TSMC secures an agreement to build and operate the facility using its own manufacturing nodes, Intel’s 14A technology could be pushed out of the equation entirely.
Article Summary: Elon Musk confirms talks with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) about Terafab semiconductor plant. Report claims that TSMC is interested in establishing a dedicated chip manufacturing plant focused entirely on supplying Musk’s companies, including Tesla, SpaceX and artificial intelligence (AI) startup xAI. Currently, Intel is slated to deliver its 1.4-nanometer-class Intel 14A process node to manufacture semiconductors for Musk's companies.
