Article Title: In 2019, Alibaba Group co-founder Jack Ma told Elon Musk, 'Humans will always be smarter than machines': What Tesla CEO said
Article Text:
Ma says computer is one of clever tools humans created

At a time when there is an escalating debate over AI safety and the power of modern frontier models, an old video of an exchange between Elon Musk and Alibaba co-founder Jack Ma has surfaced online. The video, reposted by Musk, captures Ma doubling down on human exceptionalism, arguing that machines will never outsmart the species that invented them.“Computers may be very clever, but human beings are much smarter. We invented the computer. I've never seen a computer invent a human being,” Ma argued during their conversation at an event in Shanghai in 2019. Ma’s take was rooted in the traditional view of computing: machines are ultimately instruments. While hardware can compute equations faster and store far more data, people retain qualities that silicon cannot replicate, including life experience, nuanced judgment, and wisdom.Ma, however, acknowledged that AI can beat humans at games like chess and Go but said that computers would remain one of several clever tools that humans have developed.“Don't worry about the machines. For sure, we should understand one thing: that man can never make another man. A computer is a computer. A computer is just a toy. Man cannot even make a mosquito. So, we should have a confidence. Computers only have chips, men have the heart.It's the heart where the wisdom comes from,” he said.He concluded that “my view is that [a] computer may be clever, but human beings are much smarter”.Musk dismissed the premise immediately, posing a direct challenge: “What would be an example of something that humans are better than a computer at?”“It's going to get to the point where [AI] just can completely simulate a person in every way possible, like many people simultaneously. In fact, there's a strong argument, we're in the simulation right now," he added.
Article Summary: Alibaba co-founder Jack Ma and Tesla CEO Elon Musk had an exchange at an event in Shanghai in 2019. Ma argued that machines will never outsmart the species that invented them. Ma acknowledged that AI can beat humans at games like chess and Go but said computers would remain one of several clever tools that humans have developed.

Article Title: Meta lets go co-founders and employees of AI startup Virtue AI, four months after the company hired them; Andy Stone admits differences over style of working
Article Text:
Meta lets go co-founders and employees of AI startup Virtue AI, four months after the company hired them; Andy Stone admits differences over style of working

Meta says Virtue AI arrangement did not work out

Why Meta hired the Virtue AI team

Meta continues AI safety push

Meta is letting go of employees from an AI security startup it acquired just months ago. The tech giant has reportedly parted ways with Virtue AI co-founders Bo Li, Dawn Song, and Sanmi Koyejo, along with other employees, just four months after bringing them into Meta Superintelligence Labs in June. Meta spokesperson Andy Stone confirmed the departures to Semafor and said the arrangement did not work out as planned because of differences in working styles.The move comes after Meta had recruited the Virtue AI team to strengthen its efforts around AI safety, security and frontier risks. The startup had previously worked with companies including Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as the Commerce Department’s National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST).Meta spokesperson Andy Stone confirmed the departures to Semafor and attributed the decision to differences in how the team worked.“Unfortunately, the arrangement didn’t work out as planned,” Stone said, adding that Meta Superintelligence Labs remains focused on AI safety, alignment and frontier risk.The departures come as Meta continues to shape its AI strategy and expand its capabilities around increasingly advanced AI systems.The company has been investing heavily in artificial intelligence, while AI safety and security have also become a growing focus for technology companies and policymakers.In June, Axios reported that Meta Superintelligence Labs hired Virtue AI co-founders Bo Li, Dawn Song and Sanmi Koyejo, along with other members of the startup’s team.The hiring aimed to strengthen Meta’s security efforts around AI agents at a time when concerns about the safety of increasingly capable AI systems were growing.Virtue AI had developed enterprise AI security tools covering automated red teaming, runtime guardrails and AI governance. The startup had also previously worked with Anthropic, OpenAI and the Commerce Department’s NIST. However, the terms of the arrangement were not disclosed.“As we ship AI products to billions of people and build increasingly capable agents, keeping those systems safe, reliable, and trustworthy is foundational,” the memo says.Li and Song were set to report to Nat Friedman, a Meta Superintelligence Labs executive, while Koyejo was expected to report to Rob Fergus, head of Meta's fundamental AI research lab, FAIR.Meta's decision to bring in the Virtue AI founders reflected the company's broader push to strengthen AI security as it develops more capable models and agents.The startup's work focused on identifying potential risks in AI systems and developing tools to test and safeguard them. Its technology included automated red teaming to identify weaknesses in AI systems, as well as runtime guardrails and governance tools.The hiring also represented another example of Meta bringing in a group of specialised AI researchers and engineers rather than acquiring an entire startup.Despite the departure of the Virtue AI team, Stone said Meta Superintelligence Labs remains focused on AI safety, alignment and frontier risk.The development comes as AI companies face increasing scrutiny over how they develop, test and deploy increasingly capable systems. AI agents, in particular, have become a growing area of focus as companies work on systems that can perform more complex tasks with less human intervention.Meta's decision to recruit the Virtue AI team in June was part of that broader push. However, the arrangement lasted only four months before the company decided to let the employees go.The Virtue AI hiring was also part of Meta's broader strategy to recruit specialised teams from smaller AI companies.Meta poached the founders and team behind Dreamer, an AI startup focused on helping people build agents, in March. The approach allows the company to bring in specialised talent and expertise without necessarily acquiring an entire company.The Virtue AI departures now mark a much shorter-lived version of that strategy, with Meta confirming that differences in working styles contributed to the arrangement ending.The company, however, continues to expand its AI operations as the race to develop increasingly capable models and agents intensifies.
Article Summary: Virtue AI co-founders Bo Li, Dawn Song, and Sanmi Koyejo have been let go by Meta Superintelligence Labs. The tech giant hired the Virtue AI team in June to strengthen its efforts around AI safety, security and frontier risks. The departures come as Meta continues to shape its AI strategy.

Article Title: Apple is making changes to its OS for Macs after users' complain about Meta's AI Agent Muse accessing their 'private data'
Article Text:
Apple's complete statement on updates to Full Disk Access in macOS

Apple is planning to change its Mac operating system, and the reason are AI Agents. The company wants to make it more clear to users when AI agents ask ​to access all of the data on their Macs. The announcement comes after some users have criticized Meta's ‌Muse, an AI agent for accessing their private messages. While on ​Apple's iPhones and iPads, no single app can access data inside another ​app by default, company's Macs are ⁠more flexible. Apple Macs come with a 'Full Disk Access' option that allows apps such as cloud ​backup services to access all the data on a machine, with a user's permission.In an update posted on its developer website, Apple said that some developers were using the Full Disk Access feature in ways that could put users at risk. "Going forward, we will introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely ​wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so ​with very explicit user action," Apple wrote."As AI agents become increasingly capable and autonomous, ‌the ⁠risks associated with this level of access will grow substantially. We are committed to ensuring users clearly understand these risks before granting such access, so they can make informed decisions about their own data and privacy."Apple's announcement comes after a technology ​columnist in Inc magazine accused ​Meta's Muse of ⁠reading private messages on his Mac. "In fact, I remember explicitly choosing not to let it have access to my messages, calendar, and other personal information," he wrote. He claimed that he had not enabled Full Disk Access and further added that when he asked Muse to explain how this occurred, the AI said that it was syncing his "device notifications. " Similarly, a YouTuber named Matt Robb recently said that Muse mishandled a task in which he was selling things on Facebook Marketplace, leading to his address being shared.Meta spokesperson Andy Stone disputed the claims saying that Muse's access to Apple's Messages app ​is strictly ⁠opt-in. "You have to enable both Full Disk Access and the Messages connector for Muse to be able to read your Messages content," Stone wrote on social media platform X, opens new tab. "It ⁠can't read ​your Messages unless you do this. And it ​can be revoked at any time.""We give developers powerful APIs to build incredible capabilities into their apps for Apple products, backed by a set of controls designed to protect users’ private data. Full Disk Access largely sidesteps these controls in order to allow backup apps to function properly on the Mac. Some developers are using Full Disk Access in ways that could put users at risk, exposing everything on their systems -- including files, mail, messages, and even browsing history -- without users’ full knowledge and understanding. For communication apps, this can also compromise the privacy of the people users are communicating with.""Going forward, we will introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action. Addressing this is critical. As AI agents become increasingly capable and autonomous, the risks associated with this level of access will grow substantially. We are committed to ensuring users clearly understand these risks before granting such access, so they can make informed decisions about their own data and privacy. "
Article Summary: Apple is planning to change its Mac operating system, and the reason are AI Agents. The company wants to make it more clear to users when AI agents ask ​to access all of the data on their Macs. The announcement comes after some users have criticized Meta's ‌Muse, an AI agent for accessing their private messages.

Article Title: In 2023, a London house-clearance crew found two old computers buried under boxes; they were two of only three known surviving Q1 microcomputers, and the 1972 model later sold for £37,179
Article Text:
In 2023, a London house-clearance crew found two old computers buried under boxes; they were two of only three known surviving Q1 microcomputers, and the 1972 model later sold for £37,179/Image: Heritage Auctions via SWNS​

Computers that predated the Apple 1

Rare machines went on public display

First auction made value uncertain

The world's first fully integrated desktop computer was found among boxes during a London house clearance in 2023, with one of the rare machines later sold for £37,179 at auction. The computers were discovered by house-clearance firm Just Clear while workers were clearing a London property. The find included a 1972 Q1 desktop microcomputer with an internal printer and its slightly later sibling, the Q1 Lite.Only three Q1 microcomputers are known to have survived, which makes the two machines particularly rare. A companion printer designed for the Q1 Lite was also found during the clearance. The three devices were later offered for the first time at auction by Dallas-based Heritage Auctions. The 1972 Q1 achieved the highest price, selling for £37,179. The Q1 Lite sold for £8,316, while its companion printer fetched £1,175.All three machines were sold without a reserve.The Q1 dates back to 1972, four years before Steve Wozniak and Steve Jobs introduced the Apple 1.The machine used a microprocessor-based architecture that allowed it to deliver capabilities that had previously been associated with much larger computer systems.Valarie Spiegel, Heritage Auctions' director of video games, said the technology allowed the Q1 to “punch well above its weight” and established an important precedent for the computing industry.The Q1 was also far from affordable by the standards of the time. The machines would have cost the equivalent of more than £70,000 each, making them too expensive to be marketed for individual use.Despite that limitation, the Q1 represented an early step towards the development of computers that could eventually become part of everyday life.The computers did not go directly from the London house clearance to the auction block.The Q1, Q1 Lite and companion printer were displayed at Kingston University in London in February 2024, as part of an exhibition titled Creating the Everything Device: Showcasing the Machines That Built the Future.The exhibition focused on early computers and gaming machines and placed the newly discovered Q1s alongside other examples of early technology.Paul Neve, a senior lecturer at Kingston University, said having two Q1 machines available for the exhibition offered an opportunity to show the technology that preceded modern computers.“It is a real bonus being able to feature two Q1s, the world’s earliest microcomputers, at Kingston University,” Neve told New Atlas.He said the computers developed during the 1970s and 1980s helped establish the foundations for modern machines used for work, communication, productivity and entertainment.The Heritage sale was also significant because the machines had never previously been auctioned.Before the bidding began, Sara Balbi, managing director of Heritage Auctions' London office, said there was no established auction record for the Q1s that could indicate how much buyers might pay.“Keep in mind these have never been to auction, and there is no record or precedent set for them. We'll have to see what the market decides,” Balbi said.The eventual results put a value on the rare pieces of computing history.The 1972 Q1 with its internal printer sold for £37,179, while the later Q1 Lite reached £8,316. The separate Q1 companion printer sold for £1,175. The sale also highlighted just how scarce these early machines have become, giving collectors a rare chance to own a piece of computing history.
Article Summary: The Q1 was the world's first fully integrated desktop computer. It was found among boxes during a London house clearance in 2023. One of the rare machines later sold for £37,179 at auction. The Q1 dates back to 1972, four years before the Apple 1.

Article Title: Google pauses open-source bug bounty program after rise in AI spam submissions
Article Text:
What changes and what stays active

Read Google VRP’s post

PSA for open-source bug hunters

We are temporarily no longer accepting OSS VRP product vulnerability submissions.

This does not impact OSS VRP supply chain reports, or any outstanding reports. As an alternative, we encourage you to find impact across our other VRP programs and submit there instead, or pursue the Patch Rewards Program.

Why is this happening? This pause is due to a significant rise in automated submissions, the vast majority of which are not valid. We will continue to reformat and work on this aspect of the OSS VRP and commit to giving an update in Q1 2027.

Google has paused product vulnerability submissions for its Open Source Software Vulnerability Reward Program (OSS VRP) after a flood of invalid, AI-generated reports overwhelmed security engineers and repository maintainers. The company announced the operational freeze in a post on X, directing security researchers toward its other active reward initiatives. Google stated that it will use the downtime to restructure the submission framework, with an official progress update slated for the first quarter of 2027.The suspension took effect immediately on October 1, though Google outlined specific exceptions to avoid shutting down critical disclosure channels. One of them is that the pause does not affect valid product vulnerability filings logged before October 1. The freeze applies specifically to product vulnerability reports; supply chain disclosures submitted under the OSS VRP remain open.Certain product vulnerability reports tied to Google Cloud repositories that directly impact Cloud products may still be accepted through the separate Google Cloud VRP.Previously, Linux maintainers reported being completely flooded by bogus Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) filings after automated AI hunters drove recorded vulnerabilities to a record high of 2,000 per release. The influx forced the Linux project to drop support for older network drivers.Chipmaker Intel also recently froze its bug bounty program, which offered payouts reaching $100,000 per flaw. While Intel did not cite synthetic submissions as the official cause, industry analysts widely attribute the shutdown to identical AI spam bottlenecks.
Article Summary: Google has paused product vulnerability submissions for its Open Source Software Vulnerability Reward Program. The company announced the operational freeze in a post on X, directing security researchers toward its other active reward initiatives. Google stated that it will use the downtime to restructure the submission framework, with a progress update slated for the first quarter of 2027.

Article Title: Is Minecraft Dungeons 2 cross platform? Crossplay and multiplayer explained
Article Text:
Minecraft Dungeons II officially supports cross-platform (Image via Mojang)

Is Minecraft Dungeons 2 crossplay?

How co-op works in Minecraft Dungeons II

Turning on Cross-platform in Minecraft Dungeons II

Launch Minecraft Dungeons II and go to the main menu.

Open Settings and look for the Game options section.

Find Cross-Platform Play and toggle it on.

Crossplay vs. Cross-Progression

Subscription requirements

Minecraft Dungeons II launched on September 29, 2026, and the new dungeon crawler has received a solid reception from the community. For anyone planning to squad up with friends across different consoles, the good news arrived early: crossplay is fully supported.If you are looking for further details, you are at the right place. Here's a breakdown of how multiplayer works, what crossplay actually covers, and what to know before jumping into a session.Yes. Minecraft Dungeons II supports cross-platform play across every system it launched on: PC, Xbox, PlayStation, and Nintendo Switch, for parties of up to four players. This builds on a feature the original Minecraft Dungeons already had, so Mojang carried the functionality forward into the sequel rather than building it from scratch.Official store listings and Xbox have both confirmed cross-platform multiplayer and cross-platform co-op, meaning a group spread across PlayStation, Xbox, Switch, and PC can all land in the same session without workarounds. Mojang hasn't published a detailed platform-by-platform compatibility chart, so the exact mechanics of every possible pairing aren't fully spelled out.Minecraft Dungeons II supports up to four players at once, whether that's entirely online, entirely local couch co-op, or a mix of both happening in the same session.That hybrid option, officially called Mixed Co-Op, is one of the sequel's standout multiplayer additions, since the original game required players to choose one mode or the other rather than blending them.Joining a session works two ways: through matchmaking, which fills empty slots automatically, or by sharing an eight-character party code with friends so they can join a specific lobby directly, regardless of what platform they're on.Cross-platform play is tied to account sign-in rather than being fully automatic. To enable it:Once enabled, the setting stays active going forward unless manually turned off from the same menu.It's worth separating two related but different features. Crossplay lets players on different platforms share a session together. Cross-progression is about carrying a saved character from one platform to another. Mojang has confirmed that hero data is stored online rather than locally, so progress follows players who sign in with the same Microsoft account across devices.Online console multiplayer isn't entirely free of extra requirements. Xbox players need an active Game Pass tier that includes online multiplayer, while PlayStation players need an active PlayStation Plus subscription to play online. PC players don't need anything beyond owning the game, and it's also available through Game Pass on day one as an Xbox Play Anywhere title.To conclude it all, squads spread across different consoles can enjoy Minecraft Dungeons II together. Now you can easily jump into a friend's game using party codes and have a blast playing the game. The big things to double check before you go are having an active online subscription on consoles and making sure cross platform play is toggled on in settings.
Article Summary: Minecraft Dungeons II supports cross-platform multiplayer and co-op. This means a group spread across PlayStation, Xbox, Switch, and PC can all land in the same session without workarounds. Cross-progression is about carrying a saved character from one platform to another.

Article Title: From crash-test airbags to Formula E: Heron Preston’s journey with discarded materials
Article Text:
Heron Preston partners with Formula E to explore sustainable motorsport fashion

From sanitation uniforms to Formula E: Heron Preston gives waste a new life

Heron Preston brings crash-test airbags, recycled materials into Formula E fashion

From fashion to motorsport for Heron Preston

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Heron Preston, discarded materials are not simply waste. They can become something new. The designer has built his work around finding new uses for materials that are often overlooked. Now, that approach is coming to motorsport through a creative partnership with Formula E, where fashion, performance and sustainability will come together. The partnership will explore how existing materials can be reused to create clothing, products and other items linked to motorsport.Heron Preston has explored the potential of unwanted materials through several projects. His 2016 UNIFORM project used upcycled decommissioned New York City Department of Sanitation uniforms and second-hand garments.More recently, he worked with Mercedes-Benz to transform crash-test airbags into garments. The clothes retained the distinctive physical qualities of the material. His approach is based on looking closely at every part of a product, from the materials used to how they are made and the people and processes involved. He calls this concept eX-Ray.ID@undefined Caption not available.Rather than simply choosing existing fabrics, eX-Ray looks at how materials can be developed and used in a more considered way.For the Formula E partnership, Heron Preston is using recycled cotton made from pre-consumer factory off-cuts and production scraps. The materials are sorted, shredded and re-spun into new yarn before being developed into a heavyweight, tightly woven fabric. The idea fits with Formula E’s own focus on recovering and reusing resources.While Preston turns recovered materials into new designs, Formula E uses regenerative braking to recover energy and use it again for racing. Together, the two sides want to explore how this thinking can be applied to motorsport fashion from the beginning of the design process.The partnership will look at more than clothing. The partners hope to explore performance wear, fan merchandise, accessories and products made from upcycled materials drawn from the sport. They also want to find new uses for components and materials after their life in racing.The GEN4 car provides an example of Formula E’s approach. It is designed to be 100% recyclable or reusable, with at least 20% recycled materials across key components.Talking about the same, Heron Preston said, “This creative partnership is about rethinking what motorsport fashion can be. I’ve always been interested in taking materials, processes and ideas from unexpected places and finding new ways to give them purpose. Working with Formula E gives me the opportunity to bring that approach into a world where performance is everything. We’re looking at how apparel can be thoughtfully designed from the material up, balancing function, quality and a more considered approach to how things are made.The partnership will be previewed at ComplexCon Los Angeles on October 3 and 4. The event will feature an exploration of eX-Ray materials and a GEN4 Formula E car with an exclusive Preston-designed livery.Ellie Norman, Chief Marketing Officer, Formula E, said, “Heron and Formula E share a curiosity about how things work and how they can be made better. In racing, we push for greater performance while using energy and materials more efficiently. Heron brings a complementary perspective, exploring what existing materials can become through design. This partnership gives us the opportunity to develop those ideas together and apply them to the products people wear. ComplexCon is the first look at that shared ambition, with the potential to build a more considered approach to motorsport fashion over time.”Also read: Formula E, Heron Preston join hands to bring recycled materials to motorsport fashion
Article Summary: Designer Heron Preston partners with Formula E to explore sustainable motorsport fashion. The partnership will explore how existing materials can be reused to create clothing, products and other items linked to motorsport. Preston has previously worked with Mercedes-Benz to transform crash-test airbags into garments.
